findings.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose Location is not in source (Location.None or null location). Previously diagnostics created with a null/None location, such as MemberNeedsKey (MsgPack004) for an inherited member from a base type in a referenced assembly, or other reports using GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation that can return null, were still reported. Now they are silently suppressed, so users stop seeing MsgPack003/004/005 etc. in their builds. That is a behavior change beyond the metadata-struct crash fix.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test: a [MessagePackObject] class in the compiling assembly derives from a base class in a referenced assembly that has a public property without [Key]. Run on base and head and compare MsgPack004 diagnostics. Head should drop the diagnostic if it was previously reported with Location.None or a derived location.

findings.claim: The new early return skips every generic type whose OriginalDefinition is in metadata, including those that previously went through CollectGeneric and registered closed generic formatters. Examples are generic [MessagePackObject] types from a referenced assembly, and generic types handled by the dynamic/resolver paths (for example ones with custom formatters or collection-like generics handled later). The return sits before the `type.IsDefinition` check, so it may also change which formatters or resolver entries are generated for closed generic classes from referenced assemblies, which the requirement says must keep working as before (the 'class Item<T> ok' rows). A generated resolver's output could change.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator snapshot tests, and add a case where a referenced assembly defines generic class Item<T> and the compiling assembly has a member of type Item<int>. Compare the generated resolver on base vs head for any dropped formatter registration or ResolverRegisterInfo.
